extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies, agency rulewriters, and members of the public submitting comments
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and procedural requirements for federal regulatory planning, retrospective review of existing rules, and guidance on what makes effective public comments under Executive Order 13563 (2011).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect public health, welfare, safety, and environment while promoting economic growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations should safeguard health, welfare, safety, and the environment, while also promoting economic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory objectives must balance protective goals with economic considerations; rulemaking should seek outcomes that protect core public interests without unnecessarily impeding economic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be based on the best available science
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations must rely on the best available scientific evidence when addressing public health, safety, welfare, or environmental concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency actions should cite and apply the best available science; public comments supporting or challenging rules should cite relevant scientific sources. (Also reflected in advice to 'cite best available science' under implications for comments.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow for public participation and open exchange of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The rulemaking process must provide opportunities for public participation and an open exchange of information and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations 'shall be adopted through a process that involves public participation' including input from State, local, and tribal officials, experts, affected private-sector stakeholders, and the public. Agencies should design notice-and-comment procedures to solicit and consider this broad input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote predictability and reduce uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory actions should foster predictability for regulated parties and reduce uncertainty about regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft rules and accompanying analyses should make clear obligations, timelines, and expectations to minimize ambiguity that could hinder compliance or investment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the best, most innovative, and least burdensome tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should select regulatory approaches that are effective, innovative where appropriate, and impose the least burden necessary to achieve objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider flexible, market-based, performance-based, or other innovative mechanisms that achieve goals with lower burdens; public comments should suggest feasible, less burdensome alternatives when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take into account benefits and costs, including non-quantifiable values
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulators must consider both benefits and costs of rules and explicitly account for non-quantifiable values such as equity, human dignity, and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory analyses should include quantified benefit-cost assessment where possible and narrative treatment of non-quantifiable values. Effective comments should engage with both cost and benefit dimensions and acknowledge qualitative values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure regulations are accessible, consistent, written in plain language, and easy to understand
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory text and supporting materials must be clear, consistent across documents, and written in plain language understandable to affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should draft rules in plain language; commenters should 'use plain language (model the standard the rule is held to)' and point out unclear or inconsistent provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective review: develop a Preliminary Plan on the Retrospective Review of Existing Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are directed to develop and implement a Preliminary Plan that describes the agency's approach for periodically reviewing existing regulations to determine if they should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan should outline methods and schedules for review, identify candidate regulations for review, and consider burdens and benefits over time. Comments can address whether existing rules should be modified or repealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt regulations through inclusive processes with State, local, and tribal input
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking should explicitly involve State, local, and tribal officials alongside federal stakeholders and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage relevant subnational governments and tribal authorities early and substantively; public comments incorporating state/local/tribal perspectives are especially valuable where impacts are localized or jurisdiction-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective public comments should engage with cost AND benefit dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are most useful when they analyze or provide evidence on both the costs and benefits associated with a proposed regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative estimates where possible, or reasoned qualitative assessments, to help agencies assess tradeoffs; avoid comments that assert positions without addressing costs/benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective public comments should acknowledge non-quantifiable values (equity, fairness, human dignity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters should identify and discuss values that cannot easily be monetized but are relevant to regulatory decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how proposed rules affect distributive impacts, fairness, dignity, or equity even when those impacts are not captured in monetary analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective public comments should suggest more flexible, less burdensome alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than only criticizing a proposal, commenters should propose practicable, less burdensome regulatory alternatives that achieve policy objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete alternative mechanisms (e.g., performance standards, phased compliance, safe-harbor approaches) and explain how they reduce burden while meeting goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective public comments should cite best available science
rubrics_metrics.description: When addressing technical or scientific aspects of a rule, comments should reference the best available scientific literature and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations, data, reproducible analyses, or references to authoritative studies to support scientific claims in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective public comments should incorporate state/local/tribal perspectives where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that reflect on-the-ground perspectives of subnational jurisdictions or tribal governments enrich agency understanding of local impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include jurisdiction-specific data, descriptions of implementation challenges, or local stakeholder input to make comments more actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective public comments should address whether existing rules should be modified or repealed
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the retrospective review mandate, commenters should evaluate whether current regulations remain necessary and suggest modifications or repeals where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of outdated, ineffective, or unduly burdensome regulations and propose specific revisions or deletions as part of the retrospective review process.
